Let
\[
\mathbf a=(x,20),\qquad \mathbf b=(30,y),\qquad \mathbf c=(40-x,50-y).
\]
Then
\[
\sqrt{x^2+400}=|\mathbf a|,\quad
\sqrt{y^2+900}=|\mathbf b|,\quad
\sqrt{x^2+y^2-80x-100y+4100}=|\mathbf c|.
\]
By the triangle inequality,
\[
|\mathbf a|+|\mathbf b|+|\mathbf c|\ge |\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c|.
\]
Now
\[
\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c=(x+30+40-x,\;20+y+50-y)=(70,70),
\]
so
\[
|\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c|=\sqrt{70^2+70^2}=70\sqrt2.
\]
Equality occurs when the three vectors are parallel in the same direction. Taking \(x=20\) and \(y=30\) gives
\[
\mathbf a=(20,20),\quad \mathbf b=(30,30),\quad \mathbf c=(20,20),
\]
so equality is achieved.

Thus the minimum value is
\[
\boxed{70\sqrt2}.
\]
